description: Sync a Twilio account's SMS and MMS messages, voice calls with Twilio's transcriptions, conferences and debugger alerts, one document each.
opening: Sync the communication logs of one Twilio account and the subaccounts its credentials can reach. Each SMS or MMS message, each voice call, each conference and each debugger alert is one document. A call includes the text of Twilio's own transcriptions of its recordings. HydraDB does not transcribe audio, and recordings and MMS media files are not downloaded.

Twilio permissions are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Phone numbers are searchable text, not people. Items that disappear from Twilio are not removed by a routine sync.

connect.auth: Twilio uses your Account SID and Auth Token.

settings.name: messages_update_overlap_hours
settings.text: Hours of message history each sync reads again to catch later changes, such as a new delivery status. Sent as a string. 168 by default. `0` turns the overlap off.

settings.name: recordings_update_overlap_hours
settings.text: Hours of recording history each sync reads again to catch later changes. Sent as a string. 24 by default. `0` turns the overlap off.

advanced_settings.name: user_agent
advanced_settings.text: The user agent sent to Twilio. A default is set.

steps.title: Copy your credentials
steps.text: In the Twilio console, copy the Account SID and Auth Token.

steps.title: Select the account
steps.text: HydraDB offers one resource that covers the whole account. Select it to sync.

connect.account: One connector reads one Twilio account, plus every subaccount its credentials can reach. You cannot pick subaccounts one by one.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Messages are found by send time. Calls, conferences and alerts are found by their last update. After the first sync, each sync also reads the last `messages_update_overlap_hours` of messages again.
sync.edits: A message update, such as a new delivery status, is caught when it happens inside the overlap. An update to a call that ended long ago is not guaranteed to be picked up. A new recording or transcription does not on its own update a call that is already synced. A change to a message's media or a conference's participants updates that message or conference.
sync.deletes: Messages, calls, conferences and alerts that disappear from Twilio can stay searchable in HydraDB.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.twilio_sid
shared_attributes.text: The message, call, conference or alert SID. Picks out one item. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Messages
documents.title: The message text, or `Twilio message` and its SID. Search matches the message text, not this title.
documents.text: `SMS` with the direction, then `From:` with the sending number and `to` with the receiving number, then the message text, then `Media:` with each attachment's content type. The send time is written as a Sent line when Twilio reports one.
documents.date: When the message was sent, else when it was created, else when it was last updated.
documents.files: MMS media is listed by content type. The files are not downloaded.

attributes.name: from
attributes.text: The sending number. It is text only and is not attached as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: to
attributes.text: The receiving number. It is text only and is not attached as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.text: The direction, such as `inbound` or `outbound-api`.

attributes.name: sent_at
attributes.text: When the message was sent, written as the Sent line when present.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When Twilio created the message. The result date when the send time is missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the message last changed. The result date only when the send and creation times are both missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The delivery status, such as `delivered` or `failed`. It is not searchable and not a filter.

attributes.name: media_count
attributes.text: How many media items came with the message.

documents.name: Calls
documents.title: `Call`, the direction and the phone numbers that are available. With no numbers, `Twilio call` and its SID.
documents.text: `Call` with the direction, `From:` and `To:` numbers, `Status:`, `Duration:` in seconds, `Caller:` and `Answered By:`. Then `Transcript:` with the text of every Twilio transcription of the call's recordings. The creation time is written as a Started line. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the call started, else when it was created, else when it was last updated.
documents.files: None. Recordings are not downloaded. Only Twilio's own transcription text is used.

attributes.name: from
attributes.text: The caller's number, formatted when available. In the title and the text. Not attached as a person.

attributes.name: to
attributes.text: The called number. In the title and the text. Not attached as a person.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.text: The call's direction. In the title and the text.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The call status, such as `completed`, `no-answer` or `busy`, written as the Status line.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.text: The call length in seconds, written as the Duration line.

attributes.name: start_time
attributes.text: When the call started. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When Twilio created the call record, written as the Started line. It can differ from the actual start. The result date when the start time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the call record last changed. The result date only when the start and creation times are both missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: end_time
attributes.text: When the call ended.

attributes.name: has_transcript
attributes.text: Whether transcription text was included.

documents.name: Conferences
documents.title: The conference's friendly name, or `Twilio conference` and its SID.
documents.text: `Status:`, `Region:` and `Ended:` with the reason, then `Participants:` with each participant's label and call SID. The creation time is written as a Started line. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the conference was last updated, else when it was created.

attributes.name: participants
attributes.text: The participants' labels, written as the Participants line. The graph records each as a participant, by label, not by email address.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The conference status, written as the Status line.

attributes.name: started_at
attributes.text: When the conference was created, written as the Started line.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the conference last changed. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the conference was created. The result date when the update time is missing. Not searchable as its own field, though the same time is the Started line.

documents.name: Alerts
documents.one_document: One Twilio debugger alert, an error or a warning.
documents.title: The alert text, or `Twilio alert` and its SID.
documents.text: The alert text, then `Level:`, `Error code:`, `Request:` with the method and URL, and `More info:` with a link. The alert SID is written as a Key line, the log level as Status and Priority lines, and the time as a Created line. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the alert was last updated, else when it was generated.
documents.link_back: The alert's address in Twilio's API.

attributes.name: SID
attributes.text: The alert's SID, written as the Key line.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The log level, written as the Status line.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: The log level, written as the Priority line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the alert was generated, else when Twilio created it, written as the Created line. The result date when the update time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the alert last changed. Not searchable.

example_searches: Which outbound calls went unanswered yesterday?
What did the caller say on the recorded support call this morning?
What errors did our Twilio account raise about the request URL?

graph.connections: The connector creates no links. A call is not linked to its conference or recordings: transcription text is part of the call document.
people: Phone numbers are text only. They are not attached as people.
graph.from_text: Message text, call details and transcripts, conference details and alert text.

not_synced: Recording audio and MMS media files.
Transcripts of recordings that Twilio did not transcribe. HydraDB does not transcribe audio.
Phone number inventories, balances, keys, usage records, addresses, applications, queues and other account configuration.
Deletions: items that disappear from Twilio can stay in HydraDB.
